deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematical derivation. It is a heavily corrected pencil draft of a letter in German. The draft answers an inquiry forwarded 'durch Herrn Professor Betti' (Enrico Betti, Riemann's Pisa friend; the name reading is plausible). The correspondent wanted bibliographic and historical 'Nachweisungen' about what Riemann calls the Dirichlet principle.

Content, reconstructed from the image:

(1) Definition. By 'Dirichlet's principle' Riemann means a method for proving that a function is completely determined by a given partial differential equation and given linear boundary conditions. Determined means that the problem of finding a function under conditions of this kind is solvable and has one and only one solution.

In modern terms: to solve Δu = 0 in a region G with u = f on ∂G, minimise the Dirichlet integral D[u] = ∫_G |∇u|^2 dx. The Euler–Lagrange equation of D is Δu = 0. Existence comes from the (then assumed) attainment of the infimum. Uniqueness comes from convexity: if u1 and u2 are both minimisers, then D[u1 − u2] = 0, so u1 − u2 is constant, and it vanishes on the boundary.

(2) Priority. The method was applied by William Thomson in his 'Note sur une équation aux différences partielles …' (Liouville's Journal t. 12, 1847, p. 493). It was also applied by Kirchhoff in his paper on the vibrations of an elastic plate (Crelle 40, 1850). Both came after Gauss had already treated a problem that can be regarded as a special case. That is Gauss's 'Allgemeine Lehrsätze in Beziehung auf die im verkehrten Verhältnisse des Quadrats der Entfernung wirkenden Anziehungs- und Abstossungskräfte' (1840), Art. 29–34, the minimisation argument for the equilibrium distribution of mass/charge on a surface.

(3) Naming. Riemann says he named the method after Dirichlet because he had learned that Dirichlet used it in his lectures (on forces acting inversely as the square of distance). He refers the applications to his own essay 'Über die Bestimmung einer Function [einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse] durch Grenz- und Unstetigkeitsbedingungen'. That is the preliminary section of 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857), where the principle is stated and used.

(4) Lower fragments. There are fragmentary sentences about his dissertation, apparently quoting someone's judgment that his method was preferable and 'weiter führe'. A crossed-out 'Beilagen' appears. A closing paragraph mentions enclosing, or referring to, his own notes and notes of his auditors from his lectures.

No computation is present. The prime-counting numerics on the next page are unrelated to this letter.
errors: No mathematical errors, since the page contains no mathematics.

Historical remark: the principle as Riemann states it (existence of a minimiser of the Dirichlet integral) was not rigorously justified. Weierstrass's 1870 objection showed this, and it was later rescued by Hilbert (1900). The letter does not address this.
Possible slip in the attribution phrasing: in the draft, the title 'Note sur une équation aux différences partielles' is attached near Kirchhoff, but it is Thomson's note in Liouville t. 12.

results.what: Statement that a boundary value problem for a linear PDE with linear boundary conditions is uniquely solvable, proved by minimising an energy integral
results.modern_name: Dirichlet principle (variational method for the Dirichlet problem)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss 1840, Thomson 1847, Kirchhoff 1850, Dirichlet (lectures); named by Riemann 1851/1857

results.what: Riemann's own account of why he named the principle after Dirichlet and of its priority (Gauss Art. 29–34, Thomson, Kirchhoff)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (naming, in Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen 1857)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a letter draft about the history of the Dirichlet principle. The facts (Gauss, Thomson, Kirchhoff, Dirichlet's lectures, Riemann's naming) are well known, and Riemann's naming is documented in his 1857 paper. The draft is a modest archival detail of historiographic interest: it gives Riemann's own explicit priority statement and the citation of Gauss Art. 29–34. It is not new mathematics.

transcription_corrections: '(Allgemeine Lehrsätze Bd. 29 - 34.)' should read 'Art. 29–34': article numbers of Gauss's 1840 'Allgemeine Lehrsätze', not volumes.
'worden, nach dem Grundsatz[?] … eine Aufgabe' is more plausibly 'worden, nachdem Gauss schon eine Aufgabe, welche als ein specieller Fall dieser Aufgabe betrachtet werden kann, … behandelt hatte'.
'in seiner Note sur une equation aux différences partielles' refers to William Thomson's note (Liouville t. 12, p. 493), not to Kirchhoff.

'Gewährt' should be lower-case 'gewährt' (the sentence reads 'wird auf dessen Bitte [mir das Vergnügen] gewährt, die gewünschten Nachweisungen zu geben'); 'Betti' is a plausible but uncertain reading.
'Ende 1847' is uncertain; the context is Dirichlet's Berlin lectures, which Riemann attended 1847–49.
The essay title 'Über die Bestimmung einer Function durch Grenz- und Unstetigkeitsbedingungen' corresponds to the preliminary section of Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (1857).
